I'm creating some magic items for my players and I want to make sure they'd only be getting something that is below the "rare" status and decent enough to where they'd want to keep it for a while.

  1. Talisman of Orcish Bloodlust: This allows the Barbarian to continue his rage as a bonus action if it would otherwise end this turn due to either not being attacked or not attacking. Only usable once per day.

  2. Amulet of Spell Storing: This allows the wearer to store a spell up to the wearers max level spell minus one. So if the highest level spell the wearer can cast is 5, then the highest level spell the amulet will hold is 4. Once the spell is expended, it cannot expend another spell until the next day.

  3. Shadow Dart: This dart grants advantage on attack rolls if the attacker is in dim light or darkness. If the attacker AND defender are in dim light or darkness, then the range of the dart is as far as the attacker can see. The dart is usable in this way only once per day. This is for the Shadow Monk in our group. I'm actually thinking about having him spend 1 Ki point in order to utilize the shadow range property.
Rate The Rarity Of These Three Homebrew Magic Items

1. Give the option for a single Reckless Attack (tied to the same use as extending the Rage) so that it's not useless for non-barbarians.

  2. I would have someone be able to store any spell into it for two spell slots of that level, and it is stored for 12 hours. Anyone can use the stored spell, using the modifier of the original caster. The catch is, it uses the CURRENT USER'S proficiency with magic, not the caster's. This way, it's relevant to non-casters, but at the cost of having worse spells.

  3. Can activate once per day at the cost of a level 2 spell slot, 2 ki points, or 1 hit die. Activation lasts until the start of your next turn, and creates a 5 ft radius of magical darkness for that time. This is enough to hide a medium sized creature. While activated, it has advantage to hit as long as both attacker and target are in the darkness. If the Shadow Dart hits a target, the Darkness effect is absorbed into the target, blinding them until the end of your next turn.

Now your monk can choose where he teleports!

The Amulet of Spell Storing is fine as-is. Your Shadow Dart is fine, just a bit bland without the use of poisons. The Talisman is boring and needs work, as it feels like you're just trying to cater to a specific character, which is bad.
Those are great ideas, but why would I make some of the items usable by other characters if it's not what they'd be interested in?

For subtlety/characterization's sake.

If I had a barbarian that wanted a ranged weapon, and I made a returning throwing weapon that can only be used by characters while they are raging, it would be so damn specific that it breaks common sense.

Keep your abilities generic. Your players should feel like people, not the paragons that the entire world has been built for. Make useless items (crossbows, throwing axes) show up, or armor that nobody wants to wear (like platemail or small-sized armor). Make the players feel like there's more to the universe than them.

My changes to the amulet give the feeling that they allow someone to tap into their rage temporarily (like a barbarian does) or improve the ability if they already can (like barbarians).

The pendant changes allow it to be used between allies as a way to modify their playstyle. Now you can charge it with a Jump spell for your monk, or a Expeditious Retreat for your barbarian, or a random Magic Missile to use as a last ditch effort. The original would work fine, only because mages make up half of the roster.

The original shadow dart was fine as well, I just modified it so that a monk could get more use out of it than anybody (makes sense if it was made by some "Shadow Monastery" or some shit.

What I like to do is throw generic stuff at my players and let them decide on how they should use it, or useless specific stuff (like an orb only Warlocks can use with a warlock-less party) so that they can sell it or find an eccentric use for it. If the players want something specific to them, give them a magic bazaar so that they can find specific stuff for specifically them.

What are the chances of a barbarian, monk, and wizard all finding items specific to barbarians, monks and wizards while hunting kobolds?

Good point. Thanks!

What would you deem the rarity of your versions of those items? Right now they're level three so they should only be finding uncommon stuff.

The barbarian one is the only one I would say is balanced for level 3. It's really not a huge deal, even with my upgrade. The rest are all really solid, and I would say at least rare, especially considering the fact that they're relevant to late-game. Being able to give your allies spells? I can't even begin to guess what a Druid could do with that thing. And the Shadow Dart adds temporary stealth and an almost guaranteed (advantage on hit) blind, while giving Shadow Monks something to make them even more bullshit.

Oh, reduce the Ki cost of the Shadow Dart to 1 and the health cost to a flat 5. It makes it comparable to normally using Darkness as a Shadow Monk, and the flat cost is to prevent mages from feeling comfortable relying on their weak hit-die.
